title: FastGL: A GPU-Efficient Framework for Accelerating Sampling-Based GNN Training at Large Scale
problem: Sampling-based GNN training frameworks have efficiency bottlenecks across three phases: subgraph sampling, memory IO, and computation. Irregular data access patterns and synchronization overhead limit performance when training on billion-scale graphs.
motivation: Training GNNs on large graphs with billions of nodes and edges is practically important, but existing frameworks suffer from efficiency limitations that prevent optimal GPU utilization.
method: FastGL optimizes all three training phases simultaneously: (1) Match-Reorder strategy exploits graph structure overlap to reduce memory data traffic without GPU memory overhead, (2) Memory-Aware computation leverages GPU memory hierarchy to mitigate irregular data access, (3) Fused-Map approach reduces synchronization overhead during sampling. The techniques are coordinated to account for GPU characteristics and graph structure properties.
key_novelty: Match-Reorder strategy that exploits inherent graph structure overlap to reduce memory data traffic without GPU memory overhead.
contributions: Identification of three distinct bottlenecks in sampling-based GNN training pipelines
Match-Reorder strategy for reducing memory IO by exploiting graph structure overlap
Memory-Aware computation method leveraging GPU memory hierarchy for irregular access
Fused-Map approach to reduce synchronization overhead in sampling

metrics.speedup: 11.8× over PyG, 2.2× over DGL, 1.5× over GNNLab
